brewing.notes: A safe starting point for black tea: Western style, water just off the boil.

description:
Another Chinese name for Lapsang Souchong, the pine-smoked black tea of the Wuyi Mountains in Fujian, centred on Tongmu.

Treat it as you would any black tea: water just off the boil, a few minutes in the pot, and a seller who can say where it was grown.
history: The tea dates from around the Ming-Qing transition. By legend, soldiers passing through the Wuyi area delayed the processing of fresh leaves, and farmers rescued them by drying them over pine; this story is not confirmed as history. The name Zhengshan Xiaozhong appears before 1640. An unsmoked version arose in Tongmu in the early 21st century.
processing: Leaves are smoke-dried over a pinewood fire, by cold smoking during processing or hot smoking afterwards.
harvest_season: Picked through the growing season, as with most black teas.
taste_profile: Pine smoke and resin with a note of dried longan.
vintage_note: Black teas are normally sold by harvest year and are best within a couple of years.
